title: Indefinite objects: plural partitive
summary: Choose plural partitive for an unspecified number of things being bought.
objectives: Choose plural partitive for an unspecified number of things being bought.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Choose plural partitive for an unspecified number of things being bought.
The plural partitive leaves the collection open: it does not identify a complete, previously specified set. The English plural matters, even when English does not include the word some.
Use the complete noun forms shown. Plural stems outside the regular -ja/-jä family are supporting forms here.
keyPoints: An unspecified number of countable objects uses plural partitive in this purchasing pattern.

steps: An unspecified number of countable objects uses plural partitive in this purchasing pattern.
Ostan means “I buy” and works as the verb. ostan comes from ostaa: osta- + -n.
leluja means “toys” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep lelu and add -ja: lelu + ja = leluja.
An unspecified number of countable objects uses plural partitive in this purchasing pattern.
Ostan means “I buy” and works as the verb. ostan comes from ostaa: osta- + -n.
palloja means “balls” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep pallo and add -ja: pallo + ja = palloja.
An unspecified number of countable objects uses plural partitive in this purchasing pattern.
Ostan means “I buy” and works as the verb. ostan comes from ostaa: osta- + -n.
kirjoja means “books” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Replace final a with o, then add -ja: kirjo- + -ja = kirjoja.
An unspecified number of countable objects uses plural partitive in this purchasing pattern.
Ostan means “I buy” and works as the verb. ostan comes from ostaa: osta- + -n.
kuppeja means “cups” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Change final i to e and keep strong pp: kuppe- + -ja = kuppeja.

commonMistakes: A nominative plural can identify a complete set; that is not the requested open collection.
Preserve the plural meaning even when English omits some.
